also_verified_on: 1.0.1-R2006.1 (identical but for the `--reasoning-effort` value list: no `max`), 1.1.0-R2009.1 and 1.1.0-R2074.1 (muse-canary; R2074.1: no `max` either, `exec --max-tool-output-bytes` help gains `(0 or >=9)`) — docs/experiments/stable-1.0.3-diff.md 1.3.0-R3057.1 (new top-level `mcp`: OAuth login/logout for streamable-HTTP MCP servers) — docs/experiments/stable-1.3.0-diff.md
gated_rule: `counts.gated` counts commands whose argv is REJECTED (exit 2) without their gate — `plugins` only (`gate_hard: true`). Four items carry a `gate` field: `schema` and `serve` sit behind MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_SDK_ENABLED, which is default ON (they only disappear when it is set to 0/false/yes/""), and `session-message` gates only its `list` verb (exit 1, not 2). verify_data holds counts.gated == items with gate_hard.
unknown_token_rule: There is NO unknown-command exit. An unrecognised first token is the [PROMPT] positional and starts a (billed) session; the outcome is 0/1 decided by workspace trust / TTY, not by the token. `omm run` must validate argv[0] against `argv_allowlist` (R20).

exit_codes.1: parsed, run failed (incl. ungated `session-message list`, `config validate` invalid, `init` on an existing AGENTS.md, unknown top-level token on a non-tty, hook block under `exec`)
exit_codes.2: argv rejected — a parse error and a missing gate (`plugins` without MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS) are indistinguishable; uniform across all five parsers incl. an unknown root flag
exit_codes.125: internal PTY-gate mode killed by timeout (not a product surface; `hr::EXIT_PTY_GATE_TIMEOUT`). omm's own budget for a wedged host is `invoke::RUN_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT` / `RUN_TIMEOUT_LONG`: the host is killed and reported as `HostError::Timeout`, never waited for.

root_flag_walk_rule: Root flags may precede ONLY `resume` (`muse [OPTIONS] [resume <session-uuid>]`); any other command after a root flag is refused by the host (`invalid TUI options: unknown argument `exec``, exit 2). Every other bare token after the root flags is the [PROMPT] positional, `--` hands the rest of argv to it, and a lone `-` is a prompt too: `muse -- hi`, `muse --provider echo hi`, `muse --provider echo -- hi`, `muse -` and a flag-only argv (`muse --provider echo`, `muse -w`) all start the TUI (measured 2026-09-02, stdin=/dev/null: TUI escape sequences, exit 1 `Device not configured`). A `<VALUE>` flag consumes the next token. A `[<VALUE>]` flag consumes the next token ONLY when it is exactly one of its listed `values`: measured 2026-09-02 in a pty (git workspace, `--provider echo --yolo`), `muse -w off zebra` and `muse -w create zebra` take the mode and submit `zebra` as the prompt, `muse -w zebra` creates the worktree (bare `-w` = create) AND submits `zebra` (8 screen mentions, 5 in session.jsonl; `-w` alone: 0), `muse -w OFF` leaves `OFF` to the prompt (case-sensitive), while an attached `-w=hi` / `--worktree=hi` is exit 2 `invalid value 'hi' for '--worktree'` with no session. `--version` anywhere in argv pre-empts the whole parse (`muse hi --version`, `muse -w hi --version` and `muse -w off --version` all print the version, exit 0), so an exit-0 `--version` run proves nothing about value consumption.
dispatcher_literal: execconfigexporttraceloginlogoutsession-messageskillssandboxschemaservepluginsworkflows (resume is a root positional; init/auth live in adjacent literals)

parser_families.note: `--help` works at depth 1 and 2 only. zsh gotcha: use ${=c} to word-split a subcommand string.

items.name: resume
items.help_first_line: muse resume — resume a previous session
items.notes: Accepts the entire root flag set on either side of `resume`. Non-interactive needs --last or a uuid.

items.name: exec
items.help_first_line: muse exec — run one prompt non-interactively (headless)
items.notes: --json emits MSP durable records as JSONL. Three undocumented flags: --agents, --eval-context-compaction-strategy, --eval-workflow-api-version; --api-key is recognised only to refuse it.

items.name: config
items.notes: Verbs: validate, status. Any other token reprints usage. NOT gated by MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENTERPRISE_CONFIG.

items.name: export
items.summary: Export a session transcript to a file
items.notes: Exactly four flags + --help. export_schema_version 1. Succeeds even with a malformed settings.json.

items.name: trace
items.summary: Inspect a recorded session or run trace
items.help_first_line: muse trace — inspect a recorded Muse Code trace
items.notes: Only verb: inspect (--fixture | --session-log | --run-log | --task-log, --run-id, --all-runs, --render-mode compact|default|verbose, --include-positions, --max-text-bytes, --format text|json).

items.name: skills
items.summary: List, inspect, enable, or disable skills
items.notes: See verbs.skills.

items.name: sandbox
items.summary: Check or set up the OS sandbox
items.notes: Verbs: windows check | windows setup — `windows` is the only subcommand; `check` runs on macOS and reports windows_host_required (exit 1).

items.name: schema
items.summary: Export the MSP wire schema (JSON Schema or TypeScript)
items.help_first_line: muse schema — export the MSP wire schema embedded in this binary
items.notes: Verbs: generate-json-schema --out DIR [--experimental], generate-ts --out DIR [--experimental]. Fingerprints are build-time constants.

items.name: serve
items.summary: Serve an MSP session host over stdio
items.help_first_line: muse serve — serve an MSP session host over stdio
items.notes: Flags: --no-session-log, --disable-sandbox, --sandbox-network <MODE>, --disable-write, --disable-shell, --trust-workspace. --listen parsed and refused (deferred post-v1); --yolo/--approval-* refused (approval is on the wire). Requires settings.provider; MSP runs no hooks and registers no tools.

items.name: session-message
items.notes: Verbs: list [--json]; send --target <uuid-or-name> [--in-reply-to <token>] [--json] — `send` is stubbed (`not implemented in this build`).

items.name: mcp
items.summary: Log in to or out of an MCP server (OAuth)
items.help_first_line: muse mcp — log in to or out of an MCP server (OAuth)
items.notes: Verbs: login <server> [--oauth-client-id <CLIENT_ID>] [--scope <SCOPE>]... [--headless] [--callback-port <PORT>]; logout <server> — `<server>` is a streamable-HTTP entry under mcpServers in settings.json. New in 1.3.0-R3057.1.

items.name: auth
items.help_first_line: muse auth — store provider API credentials
items.notes: Only verb: set [--provider meta] --api-key-stdin. Secrets never accepted as argv. Store: $CONFIG_DIR/auth.json or macOS Keychain (TBH_CREDENTIAL_BACKEND).

items.name: login
items.notes: Takes no arguments. NEVER run by omm (contacts Meta).

items.name: logout
items.notes: Takes no arguments.

items.name: init
items.summary: Scaffold agent config in this workspace
items.notes: Writes exactly one file, AGENTS.md; re-run without --force exits 1. Scaffolds nothing for hooks/skills/plugins.

items.name: plugins
items.notes: Ungated: prints `plugins are not available in this build`, exit 2. Appears in `muse --help` only with the gate. Runtime composition of installed plugins is ungated. See verbs.plugins.

items.name: workflows
items.summary: List/save named workflows; QA-only run/recover lane
items.notes: Never listed in any --help (self-described as unadvertised); always live; independent of MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKFLOW_TOOL. Verbs: list; save <name> --from <script.js> [--scope project|user] [--overwrite]; run <entry> --headless-qa [--token-budget <tokens|Nk|Nm>] [--live-auto-qa|--prompt-live-smoke]; recover <workflow-run-id> [--apply] (--session-log <path>|--session <id>). Project-scope workflows are never listed (no --trust-workspace flag); ship at --scope user.
one ephemeral agent-definition overlay; not on exec's help but accepted there

Value check first, provider check second: a value outside the list is exit 2 `unsupported reasoning effort `<v>`; expected <list>` (hr::REASONING_EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE); a listed value with `--provider echo` is exit 2 `--reasoning-effort is not supported with --provider echo` (hr::REASONING_EFFORT_ECHO_REFUSED_MESSAGE) — the second message proves the value was accepted, which is how hostcheck `cli/reasoning-effort/<value>` measures the list offline. `max` accepted since 1.0.3-R2198.1 (1.0.1 and canary 1.1.0-R2074.1: `unsupported reasoning effort `max``); in settings.json 1.0.1 prints `tbh: ignoring invalid reasoning_effort "max" in settings` and 1.0.3 accepts it silently with the same 8-block run context as high/xhigh; the enterprise defaults plane rejects `settings.reasoning_effort: "max"` as `semantic_invalid` on every build (1.0.3 drops the `location=` suffix from that message). `ultra` is listed on every build but gated since 1.0.3-R2198.1 (gates.json ultra_reasoning_effort).

A detached token is taken as the mode only when it is exactly one of the values (`-w off`); bare `-w` means create; any other detached token is the [PROMPT] (`-w hi` starts the TUI and submits `hi`), while `-w=hi` is exit 2 — see root_flag_walk_rule

`--available` is [] in 1.0.1/1.1.0. Does NOT emit the gate table to the bootstrap trace.

items.notes: The trust oracle: a capability line must be PRESENT and literally trusted_enabled. Kinds: hook, reminder, mcp_server, agent_definition. States: review_needed, trusted_enabled, trusted_disabled, modified, invalid, blocked.

items.notes: Non-interactive, no TTY. Stable id form plugin:<pid>:<kind>:<cap>. Writes settings.runtime_capabilities. Silently manufactures a canonical/legacy reminder conflict if settings.plugins disagrees.

Run one installed plugin hook against a fixture
items.notes: Does not require approval.

items.notes: R11 predicates: rc==0 && valid==true && diagnostics==[] && manifest_family=="native" && every compatibility declaration "supported". Zero inspection of SKILL.md. On some error paths --json is followed by a bare text line — use raw_decode.

launcher.note: `muse` on PATH is muse-launcher.sh, which exec's muse-bin-<version> and adds no subcommands. MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE / MUSE_RELEASE_INFO are launcher-only (0 occurrences in the binary). omm calls muse-bin-* directly.

process_start_validators: MUSE_WEB_SEARCH_MODE must be one of client,hosted,off — a bad value in either aborts EVERY subcommand, including --version
notes: All 16 help texts are byte-identical between 1.0.1-R2006.1 and 1.1.0-R2009.1; only --version differs (canary-diff rows 1-3).
Malformed settings.json is lazy: --version, --help, export, init, workflows list succeed; settings-consuming commands fail → probe with `muse skills list`.
There is no CLI path to persist workspace trust (no `trust` verb; --trust-workspace is per-run). trust.json must be hand-written or set in the TUI.
